column1: # Reference set -- raghavendra_2023_mix1
# Two-organism libraries, 10 pg E. coli + 2 pg S. cerevisiae, from
#   Basapathi Raghavendra J, Zorzano M-P, Kumaresan D, Martin-Torres J.
#   "DNA sequencing at the picogram level to investigate life on Mars and Earth."
# Reads: https://zenodo.org/records/8208597 ("MinION low detectability.zip"),
# fetched by bin/comparison/fetch_raghavendra.sh.
# Covers Mix1_R1 / Mix1_R2, the paper's Table 3 row
# "10 pg of E. coli + 2 pg of S. cerevisiae".
# WHY THIS EXISTS
# A re-analysis of a prior study's deposited reads under THIS pipeline's
# competitive-mapping assignment, so the prior study can be compared
# like-for-like against our numbers rather than Kraken2-against-PlusPF-8 versus
# minimap2-against-a-known-reference. See docs/comparison.md.
# NO CARRIER
# Raghavendra et al. used no genomic carrier. Methods, "Library preparation":
# "The gDNA for the nanopore library was prepared using nuclease-free water and
# the low concentration of the DNA to be tested was directly pipetted from the
# previously diluted samples" and "The whole amount of DNA ... was diluted in
# 25 ul for library preparation", with SQK-LSK114 at halved reagent volumes on
# an R10.4.1 Flongle. No lambda or other filler DNA appears anywhere in the
# paper. There is therefore no role=carrier row and carrier_dna_ng=0 in the
# samplesheet.
# ACCESSION CHOICES
# Escherichia coli -- GCA_900706755.1
#   Methods, "Test samples": "Escherichia coli (NCTC 9001 Lenticule disc, Sigma
#   Aldrich, UK) with an average genomic size of ~ 5 Mb". NCTC 9001 was
#   sequenced by the Sanger Institute's NCTC 3000 project (BioProject PRJEB6403,
#   BioSample SAMEA2517362): 5,040,580 bp in 5 contigs, N50 1,476,437 bp, which
#   corroborates the stated "~5 Mb". Exact strain, so preferred over K-12. The
#   GenBank (GCA_) accession is deliberate -- the paired RefSeq assembly
#   GCF_900706755.1 is SUPPRESSED and cannot be fetched by `datasets download`.
# Saccharomyces cerevisiae -- GCF_000146045.2 (ASSUMPTION)
#   Methods: "yeast from Saccharomyces cerevisiae, Type II (YSC-2, 51,475, Sigma
#   Aldrich) with an average genomic size of ~ 12 Mb". Sigma YSC-2 is a dried
#   commercial preparation sold by activity with no strain designation, so the
#   standard reference genome (strain S288C, assembly R64, complete,
#   12,071,326 bp, matching the stated "~12 Mb") is used and recorded as an
#   assumption rather than a strain identification.
# HOMO SAPIENS IS DELIBERATELY ABSENT
# Table 3 reports 1 and 7 human reads for these two replicates. Human is
# nevertheless not included as a contaminant reference. (1) Cost: references are
# fetched and indexed once per reference set and this study needs four sets, so
# GRCh38 would be downloaded and indexed four times. (2) Direction of the error:
# adding a competitor to a competitive assignment can only move reads AWAY from
# the target organisms, never toward them, so omitting human makes these counts
# an UPPER BOUND on the prior study -- the conservative direction with respect
# to any advantage we claim. Unmapped human reads land in the `unassigned` bin,
# which compute_metrics.py reconciles explicitly. To account for them instead:
#   Homo sapiens<TAB>GCF_000001405.40<TAB>contaminant<TAB>0<TAB>GRCh38.p14<TAB>documented cross-contamination
# theoretical_dna_fraction is by DNA mass into library prep, from the Table 3
# sample-type label (the paper states the masses directly; nothing is derived):
#   Escherichia coli          10 pg / 12 pg = 0.833333
#   Saccharomyces cerevisiae   2 pg / 12 pg = 0.166667
organism
Escherichia coli
column6: 10 pg of the 12 pg library; contig-level (5 contigs) exact strain
